regimen_profiles.clinical_summary: Capecitabine is chemotherapy taken as tablets. NCCP 00216 covers several colorectal and breast cancer settings, including treatment after surgery and treatment of advanced disease. Ask which aim and duration apply to you.
regimen_profiles.component_rationale: Capecitabine: After you swallow capecitabine, your body changes it into fluorouracil. This interferes with the DNA and RNA processes cells use to grow. Normal cells can also be affected, which helps explain mouth soreness, bowel symptoms and changes in blood counts.

eligibility_orientation: Assess counts, renal/hepatic function, symptoms and safe oral administration.
important_cautions: Complete DPD deficiency, severe prior fluoropyrimidine reaction, relevant hypersensitivity and pregnancy/lactation are exclusions.
Brivudine requires avoidance and an interval of at least four weeks before capecitabine.
The renal table differs between 00623 and 00216/00586; do not transplant dose rules.

NCCP describes caution when starting with ANC below 1.5 × 10⁹/L or platelets below 100 × 10⁹/L, while the EMA product information says not to treat at those baseline values. Reconcile the distinction before initiation; the subsequent recovery threshold of platelets at least 75 × 10⁹/L is not baseline clearance.
For haematological restart percentages, document both episode nadirs, current recovery, recurrence and the previous actual dose; current counts alone do not identify the correct row.

Dose percentages refer to the documented original starting dose, not repeated multiplication of the current reduced dose. A toxicity reduction must not be re-escalated; cautious titration of an initial partial-DPD dose is a distinct specialist exception.

At CrCl 30–50 mL/min, NCCP gives 75% of the original dose; EMA specifies that reduction for a 1250 mg/m² starting dose and no starting reduction for 1000 mg/m². Reconcile the documented starting regimen with oncology pharmacy before dosing.
Grade 3 hand-foot syndrome requires a subsequent reduction but the NCCP HFS text does not quantify it. Do not invent a universal percentage.

Stop for suspected serious skin reactions such as Stevens–Johnson syndrome/toxic epidermal necrolysis and obtain urgent specialist assessment; confirmed severe reactions require permanent discontinuation.

regimen_profiles.clinical_summary: The aim is to control advanced bowel cancer and symptoms. The team reviews how well treatment is working and whether side effects remain acceptable; there is no single fixed number of cycles for everyone.
regimen_profiles.component_rationale: Cetuximab: Cetuximab attaches to EGFR on the outside of cells and blocks some growth messages. In this bowel-cancer plan, validated extended RAS testing helps identify whether treatment is suitable. Healthy skin also uses EGFR, so skin and nail effects need early care. Oxaliplatin: Oxaliplatin makes links within DNA. These interfere with copying and repair, which can stop a cancer cell dividing. Healthy tissues can also be affected. Folinic acid: Folinic acid helps fluorouracil remain bound to an enzyme needed to make DNA. In this regimen it increases fluorouracil activity and can also increase its unwanted effects. It is not a vitamin supplement to start yourself. Fluorouracil: Fluorouracil interferes with the production and use of DNA and RNA, the instructions cells need to grow. This FOLFOX4 schedule gives a bolus followed by a 22-hour infusion on Day 1 and repeats that fluorouracil sequence on Day 2.
regimen_profiles.schedule_context: Cetuximab on Day 1 and Day 8. FOLFOX4 starts on Day 1: oxaliplatin, folinic acid and fluorouracil bolus, followed by a 22-hour fluorouracil infusion. Day 2 brings another fluorouracil bolus and a second 22-hour infusion; finish around Day 3. Your team confirms the full Day 2 prescription. Repeat every 14 days while beneficial and tolerable.
key_points: Cetuximab on Day 1 and Day 8. FOLFOX4 starts on Day 1: oxaliplatin, folinic acid and fluorouracil bolus, followed by a 22-hour fluorouracil infusion. Day 2 brings another fluorouracil bolus and a second 22-hour infusion; finish around Day 3. Your team confirms the full Day 2 prescription. Repeat every 14 days while beneficial and tolerable.
RAS-wild-type metastatic colorectal cancer; response evidence is drawn from a first-line trial.
Direct regimen-family evidence for weekly cetuximab with FOLFOX4, in the first-line trial population.
Clinical trial medians and response rates belong in the clinician evidence card; patient benefit explanations remain qualitative.
FOLFOX4 is two separate 22-hour fluorouracil infusions with a Day 2 treatment visit; do not substitute the modified FOLFOX6 46-hour pump schedule.
NCCP 00692 v2 p1 prints folinic acid on Day 1 only. A Day 2 folinic-acid dose is a prescription clarification, not an automatically inferred component.

NCCP 00692 v2 p1 permits omitting observation after two tolerated cetuximab doses, whereas current EMA Erbitux SmPC sections 4.2/4.4 require monitoring during and for at least one hour after every infusion. Reconcile this conflict with oncology pharmacy/local policy; do not automatically waive monitoring. Chemotherapy must start no earlier than one hour after cetuximab ends.
Cetuximab and FOLFOX holds can be independent; assess all component-specific toxicity and prior-dose requirements before issuing a new treatment plan.

patient_selection.treatment_intent: Control advanced cancer and symptoms; any conversion or local-treatment goal requires an explicit multidisciplinary plan.
disease_and_biomarker_context: RAS-wild-type metastatic colorectal cancer; response evidence is drawn from a first-line trial.
eligibility_orientation: Consultant-initiated plan, protocol-defined performance status, marrow and organ function, and acceptable previous-cycle toxicity.
Validated extended RAS wild-type result for the colorectal EGFR-antibody indication.
important_cautions: Apply this exact regimen’s thresholds and exclusions; shared drugs do not imply shared blood-count, bilirubin or renal-dose rules.
DPD deficiency, severe early fluorouracil toxicity or cardiac symptoms require prompt specialist action.
Severe infusion reactions, significant skin toxicity, electrolyte loss, new pulmonary symptoms and corneal symptoms require assessment.
Current EMA Erbitux requires interruption for intolerable skin reactions even below grade 3; recurrent toxicity and previous cetuximab dose reductions require specialist reconciliation.

Cetuximab skin restart requires recovery to grade 2 or less within the two-week maximum. Recurrence reference doses are 250, 200 and 150 mg/m² for the first, second and third episodes; the fourth severe episode or failed recovery requires discontinuation. Record the actual previous maintenance dose and do not automatically reload or escalate.

If ANC is below 1.5 × 10⁹/L or platelets below 75 × 10⁹/L, hold FOLFOX and check counts weekly; assess cetuximab separately. Subsequent chemotherapy decisions require recovery, duration of delay, the delayed-week nadir and actual component doses. At the four-week boundary with low counts, hold and clarify; persistent low counts beyond four weeks require discontinuation under the source.

Folinic acid is held or omitted when the fluorouracil bolus is held or omitted. Grade 4 diarrhoea gives an oxaliplatin reference of 65 mg/m² but no quantified fluorouracil reduction or recovery interval; consultant review is required, and an existing lower oxaliplatin dose must not be increased to that reference.

Neuropathy decisions use the actual dose level and function: grade 2 at the next cycle or first/second grade 3 episodes require a one-level reduction; persistent grade 3 or grade 4 requires stopping oxaliplatin. Rechallenge is only a specialist consideration after good recovery from grade 3, at one level below the dose at onset; it is not a grade 4 restart pathway.

For CrCl below 30 mL/min or dialysis, NCCP says to consider 50% of the original oxaliplatin dose, with haemodialysis within 90 minutes after administration. This requires specialist planning, not an automatic recommendation.

The fluorouracil liver table contraindicates treatment for bilirubin above 85 micromol/L or AST above 180 units/L; exact boundary values require clarification. Partial DPD deficiency requires an individual reduction, not a fixed universal percentage.

supportive_care.emetogenic_risk: Day 1 · chemotherapy and antibody: Moderate; Day 2 · FOLFOX4 fluorouracil; confirm complete prescription: Low treatment-day risk; delayed Day 1 moderate-risk coverage still applies; Day 8 · weekly cetuximab only: Low
premedication_and_prophylaxis: Give an antihistamine and a corticosteroid before every cetuximab infusion, including Day 8. NCCP suggested regimen: chlorphenamine 10 mg IV and dexamethasone 8 mg IV 60 minutes before cetuximab.

Day 1 oxaliplatin has moderate emetic risk; Day 2 fluorouracil and Day 8 cetuximab have low treatment-day risk. Reconcile the multi-day antiemetic prescription and avoid duplicate corticosteroid doses.
No routine G-CSF schedule is mandated by NCCP 00692; assess individual risk and previous complications.
Avoid cold exposure and ice chips because oxaliplatin can provoke acute neurotoxicity. Maintain skin care, electrolyte replacement when indicated, written bowel advice and line/pump support.
patient_education: Start the prescribed skin-care plan early, use moisturiser and sun protection, and report painful or infected skin or nails. Keep mineral blood-test appointments during treatment and for two months after cetuximab.
Follow your written rescue plan. Fever, blood, severe pain, reduced urine or inability to drink needs urgent advice.
Arrange Day 2 infusion renewal and final disconnection around Day 3. This is two separate 22-hour infusions; do not use a 46-hour pump timetable.

Avoid cold drinks and cold exposure as instructed after oxaliplatin; do not suck ice chips during fluorouracil in this regimen. Use prescribed anti-sickness medicines, pace activities and ask for nutritional, emotional or practical support.

Ask how and when the team will assess benefit, which blood tests continue during a pause, and what happens after the final dose. Mineral checks continue monthly for two months after the last antibody treatment.
Day 8 contains cetuximab only. Its premedicines and observation still matter, but the chemotherapy-day anti-sickness course is not automatically repeated.
special_support: Antiemetic classification refers to the active treatment day. Reconcile duplicate steroid entries before prescribing.
No automatic G-CSF schedule is added; use the patient’s neutropenia history, risk and consultant plan.
Cetuximab premedication and infusion observation remain necessary even on an antibody-only day.
Start local EGFR skin care; monitor magnesium, calcium and potassium before and periodically during therapy, then monthly for two months after the final dose.

Cold exposure can precipitate oxaliplatin neurotoxicity; do not recommend ice chips during fluorouracil in this combination. Review neuropathy every two cycles and sooner if symptoms interfere with function.
Confirm line care, pump contact details and disconnection arrangements; report chest pain, severe early fluorouracil toxicity or pump/line problems urgently.

NCCP 00692 v2 p1 permits omitting observation after two tolerated cetuximab doses, whereas current EMA Erbitux SmPC sections 4.2/4.4 require monitoring during and for at least one hour after every infusion. Reconcile this conflict with oncology pharmacy/local policy; do not automatically waive monitoring. Chemotherapy must start no earlier than one hour after cetuximab ends.
FOLFOX4 uses two separate 22-hour fluorouracil infusions on Days 1 and 2, with a second treatment visit; never substitute a single 46-hour modified-FOLFOX6 pump schedule.
Cetuximab and FOLFOX may be delayed independently. Reconcile actual treatment days, component-specific recovery and previous dose changes before updating support prescriptions.
Intolerable cetuximab skin reactions require interruption even when graded below 3 under the EMA product information; review infection and supportive skin care promptly.

NCCP 00692 v2 p1 lists fluorouracil bolus and a separate 22-hour infusion on Day 2, but lists folinic acid on Day 1 only. Confirm the intended Day 2 folinic-acid prescription with the consultant and oncology pharmacy; do not infer or silently add a Day 2 dose from a generic FOLFOX4 schedule.
No repeat cetuximab or oxaliplatin is scheduled on Day 2.
NCIS multi-day guidance: cover the risk on each administered treatment day and delayed risk after treatment, using a reconciled prescription.
Cetuximab only: no irinotecan, oxaliplatin, fluorouracil or atropine is scheduled on Day 8.
Continue skin care, electrolyte monitoring, infusion precautions and the urgent contact plan.
Low-risk antibody-only antiemesis is distinct from Day 1 moderate-risk chemotherapy prophylaxis.

Ask specifically about prior antibody infusion reactions, red-meat allergy, tick bites and any known cetuximab IgE findings.

ECG if cardiac function is compromised; no universal serial echo schedule is imposed. Confirm safe central access and pump training.

FBC, liver and renal profile before each cycle.
Repeat magnesium, calcium and potassium periodically during EGFR-antibody therapy and more frequently when abnormal; assess skin, nail, eye and pulmonary symptoms.

There is no predetermined total course: review benefit, tolerability and patient priorities, and document continuation, pause, switch or stopping decisions.
NCCP 00692 v2 requires monthly electrolytes, magnesium and calcium for two months after the last cetuximab. Current EMA Erbitux specifies baseline and periodic mineral testing during therapy.
Evaluate peripheral neuropathy every two cycles and review earlier if symptoms persist or impair function; cumulative toxicity may alter oxaliplatin independently of other components.

Infusion reaction; rare serious lung or skin effects

administration.cycle_and_sequence: Cetuximab on Day 1 and Day 8. FOLFOX4 starts on Day 1: oxaliplatin, folinic acid and fluorouracil bolus, followed by a 22-hour fluorouracil infusion. Day 2 brings another fluorouracil bolus and a second 22-hour infusion; finish around Day 3. Your team confirms the full Day 2 prescription. Repeat every 14 days while beneficial and tolerable.
route_and_duration: The first weekly cetuximab infusion takes about two hours; later weekly infusions usually take about one hour. Oxaliplatin and folinic acid are usually infused over about two hours, before fluorouracil. Blood review, preparation, premedicines and observation add time; infusion time is not the total appointment length. Allow at least one hour of monitoring after each cetuximab infusion; chemotherapy starts no earlier than one hour after cetuximab finishes. Your team confirms the final visit and observation plan. Return on Day 2 for another fluorouracil bolus and renewal of the second 22-hour infusion. The team confirms any other Day 2 medicines. Final disconnection is planned around Day 3. This FOLFOX4 plan is not a single 46-hour infusion.
practical_workflow: Confirm the exact regimen, tests, medicines, emergency number and treatment goal. Discuss which central line is suitable and arrange pump training.

Attend the separate Day 8 cetuximab-only visit. This is not another irinotecan or oxaliplatin day. Use the written symptom and support plan; do not wait for the next appointment if urgent symptoms appear.

observation_and_access: Resuscitation facilities and trained staff are required for infusions.
Allow for review, preparation and observation; quoted medicine infusion times are not total appointment times.

NCCP 00692 v2 p1 permits omitting observation after two tolerated cetuximab doses, whereas current EMA Erbitux SmPC sections 4.2/4.4 require monitoring during and for at least one hour after every infusion. Reconcile this conflict with oncology pharmacy/local policy; do not automatically waive monitoring. Chemotherapy must start no earlier than one hour after cetuximab ends.

Initial weekly cetuximab: 400 mg/m² over 120 minutes, maximum 5 mg/min. Subsequent weekly doses: 250 mg/m² over 60 minutes, maximum 10 mg/min. These are infusion times, not total appointment duration.
Agree central access, ambulatory infusion arrangements and a documented pump problem/disconnection contact plan.

evidence_at_a_glance.qualitative_result: Tumour response improved. The small extended-RAS subgroup did not establish statistically significant progression-free or overall-survival benefit.
limitations: Small retrospective subgroup; 38 combination and 49 chemotherapy-only patients.

evidence_at_a_glance.harms: Cetuximab adds EGFR-related toxicity; the chemotherapy backbone adds myelosuppression, mucositis and cumulative oxaliplatin neuropathy.
